observations: The page number «93» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01 completes the sentence that ends p. 92 (JP2 0124, L41), «ob vom Aszendenten selbst, oder von seiner». L04: «59—59b», the b raised.

A figure stands at the right of L08-L23, which are set in a narrower measure at its left; it is not reproduced. A circle, the meridian, with Z at its top, A and E at its upper left, P at its upper right, a small s beside P and a small arc marking the angle at P, H and T at the ends of a horizontal dashed diameter, K at the lower right and Q at the bottom right; dashed lines from the centre to Z, A, E, P, K and Q. Solid arcs: the horizon from H through L to T, below the diameter; the equator from A through W, D, N and R to Q; the ecliptic from E through W, L and M to K; the arcs from P through L to N and from P through M to R. W stands on the dashed diameter H T, D and N below L. The letters are italic.

L01-L07 and N01. Checked: with ε = 23° 51′ the right ascension of 228° 40′ is 226° 7′ (Table 59: 226° 10′), that of 303° 20′ 305° 43′; 305° 43′ − 226° 10′ = 79° 33′, and 305° 43′ − 226° 7′ = 79° 36′ (N01). The hour angle of the sun at 6h 44m 29s of the true time (p. 92, JP2 0124) is 78° 53′; the 40′ more are 2m 40s of time; to be compared with the equation of time of Tables 67-68.

L08-L23. Checked: with W the autumnal point, the longitude 180° + WM = 303° 20′ and the right ascension 180° + WR = 305° 43′ give WM = 123° 20′ and WR = 125° 43′. The midheaven of the example, 228° 40′, with its right ascension 226° 10′, lies 48° 40′ and 46° 10′ beyond W in the order of the signs, so that for these numbers its longitude and right ascension are 180° + WE and 180° + WA, not 180° − EW and 180° − AW as in L20-L22, which follow the figure with E and A before W; the hour angle is in either case the arc AR of the equator between the meridian and the hour circle of the moon, here WR − WA = 79° 33′. The angle APR at the pole, s, measures the arc AR.

L24-L33. Checked: 1h 33½m = 1.5583 h, and 1.5583 × 34′ 34″ = 53′ 52″, «c. 54′»; 303° 19′ 48″ + 54′ = 304° 13′ 48″. With the sine rule of the lunar equation (p. 46, JP2 0078) the hourly true motion at the anomaly 125° 7′ is 32′ 56″ + 32′ 40″ · sin 4° 56′ · |cos 125° 7′| / cos q = 34′ 33″, near the 34′ 34″ of Table 63. The table value 1h 33½m is to be compared with Table 77. N02: the moon between the ascendant and the midheaven, east of the meridian; the rule of chapter 34 of the text (p. 28, JP2 0060, L20-L21), «Si enim fuerit luna inter horoscopum et medium caelum, erit hoc productum horis coniunctionis addendum», which Suter applies to the place of the moon.

L36-L39. Checked: sin δ = sin 23° 51′ · sin 303° 20′ gives δ = −19° 44′ 39″, the 19° 44′ 38″ south of Table 22; 37° 50′ + 19° 44′ 38″ = 57° 34′ 38″, the zenith distance of the moon at its culmination. The Latin of chapter 34 (p. 28, JP2 0060, L27) asks for the declination of the midheaven, «ipsius medii caeli obliquatio»; that of 228° 40′ would be 17° 40′ south.

The note 2 has no reference in the text of the page; see the critical note. L34: «Auffinduug»; see the critical note. L26: «1h 33 1/2m», the h and m raised, the fraction small; L38: «= — 19° 44′ 38″», the minus a long dash after a space. N02: «Ascendens» with c, where the text has «Aszendent».

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.»; italics: «Rectascension» (L01), «Ascensio obliqua», «wahren Länge», «Medium Coelum» (L04, L35, L36; upright in L06, L21), «Stundenwinkel», the letters of the figure, «Längenparallaxe», «Parallaxe», «Breite», «Aszendenten», «Obliquatio», «EZ», «interstitium medii».
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (11-14 px measured).

critical_notes.evidence: the note 2 at the foot of the page, «Denn der Mond befindet sich zwischen Ascendens und Medium Coelum», gives the reason why the parallax is added to the true place of the moon; no reference to it is printed in the text
«die Regel für die Auffindung», as «die Regel für die Auffindung des Medium Coelum» (p. 92, JP2 0124, L38-L39); the n before the g is printed as u, a turned n
